ESV.1: In those days Hezekiah became sick and was at the point of death. And Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz came to him, and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Set your house in order, for you shall die, you shall not recover.”
ESV.2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
ESV.3: and said, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
ESV.4: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
ESV.5: “Go and say to Hezekiah, Thus says the LORD, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
ESV.6: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and will defend this city.
ESV.7: “This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that he has promised:
ESV.8: Behold, I will make the shadow cast by the declining sun on the dial of Ahaz turn back ten steps.” So the sun turned back on the dial the ten steps by which it had declined.
ESV.9: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, after he had been sick and had recovered from his sickness:
ESV.10: I said, In the middle  of my days I must depart; I am consigned to the gates of Sheol for the rest of my years.
ESV.11: I said, I shall not see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living; I shall look on man no more among the inhabitants of the world.
ESV.12: My dwelling is plucked up and removed from me like a shepherd's tent; like a weaver I have rolled up my life; he cuts me off from the loom; from day to night you bring me to an end;
ESV.13: I calmed myself  until morning; like a lion he breaks all my bones; from day to night you bring me to an end.
ESV.14: Like a swallow or a crane I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes are weary with looking upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my pledge of safety!
ESV.15: What shall I say? For he has spoken to me, and he himself has done it. I walk slowly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
ESV.16: O Lord, by these things men live, and in all these is the life of my spirit. Oh restore me to health and make me live!
ESV.17: Behold, it was for my welfare that I had great bitterness; but in love you have delivered my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back.
ESV.18: For Sheol does not thank you; death does not praise you; those who go down to the pit do not hope for your faithfulness.
ESV.19: The living, the living, he thanks you, as I do this day; the father makes known to the children your faithfulness.
ESV.20: The LORD will save me, and we will play my music on stringed instruments all the days of our lives, at the house of the LORD.
ESV.21: Now Isaiah had said, “Let them take a cake of figs and apply it to the boil, that he may recover.”
ESV.22: Hezekiah also had said, “What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?”

NASB.1: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. And Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz came to him and said to him, 'Thus says the LORD, 'Set your house in order, for you shall die and not live.''
NASB.2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
NASB.3: and said, 'Remember now, O LORD, I beseech You, how I have walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in Your sight.' And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
NASB.4: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
NASB.5: 'Go and say to Hezekiah, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of your father David, 'I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
NASB.6: 'I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city.''
NASB.7: 'This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that He has spoken:
NASB.8: 'Behold, I will cause the shadow on the stairway, which has gone down with the sun on the stairway of Ahaz, to go back ten steps.' So the sun's [shadow] went back ten steps on the stairway on which it had gone down.
NASB.9: A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery:
NASB.10: I said, 'In the middle of my life I am to enter the gates of Sheol; I am to be deprived of the rest of my years.'
NASB.11: I said, 'I will not see the LORD, The LORD in the land of the living; I will look on man no more among the inhabitants of the world.
NASB.12: 'Like a shepherd's tent my dwelling is pulled up and removed from me; As a weaver I rolled up my life. He cuts me off from the loom; From day until night You make an end of me.
NASB.13: 'I composed [my soul] until morning. Like a lion-- so He breaks all my bones, From day until night You make an end of me.
NASB.14: 'Like a swallow, [like] a crane, so I twitter; I moan like a dove; My eyes look wistfully to the heights; O Lord, I am oppressed, be my security.
NASB.15: 'What shall I say? For He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done it; I will wander about all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
NASB.16: 'O Lord, by [these] things [men] live, And in all these is the life of my spirit; O restore me to health and let me live!
NASB.17: 'Lo, for [my own] welfare I had great bitterness; It is You who has kept my soul from the pit of nothingness, For You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
NASB.18: 'For Sheol cannot thank You, Death cannot praise You; Those who go down to the pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
NASB.19: 'It is the living who give thanks to You, as I do today; A father tells his sons about Your faithfulness.
NASB.20: 'The LORD will surely save me; So we will play my songs on stringed instruments All [the] days of our life at the house of the LORD.'
NASB.21: Now Isaiah had said, 'Let them take a cake of figs and apply it to the boil, that he may recover.'
NASB.22: Then Hezekiah had said, 'What is the sign that I shall go up to the house of the LORD?'

AMP.1: In those days Hezekiah [king of Judah] became sick and was at the point of death. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him and said, "For the LORD says this, 'Set your house in order and prepare a will, for you shall die; you will not live.'"
AMP.2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
AMP.3: and said, "Please, O LORD, just remember how I have walked before You in faithfulness and truth, and with a whole heart [absolutely devoted to You], and have done what is good in Your sight." And Hezekiah wept greatly.
AMP.4: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying,
AMP.5: "Go and say to Hezekiah, 'For the LORD, the God of David your father says this, "I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; listen carefully, I will add fifteen years to your life.
AMP.6: I will rescue you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will defend this city [Jerusalem]."'
AMP.7: "This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will do this thing that He has spoken:
AMP.8: Listen carefully, I will turn the shadow on the stairway [denoting the time of day] ten steps backward, the shadow on the stairway ( sundial) of Ahaz." And the sunlight went ten steps backward on the stairway where it had [previously] gone down.
AMP.9: This is the writing of Hezekiah king of Judah after he had been sick and had recovered from his illness:
AMP.10:
I said, "In mid-life
I am to go through the gates of Sheol (the place of the dead),
I am to be summoned, deprived of the remainder of my years."
AMP.11:
I said, "I will not see the LORD
The LORD in the land of the living;
I will no longer see man among the inhabitants of the world.
AMP.12:
"My dwelling (body) is pulled up and removed from me like a shepherd's tent;
I have rolled up my life as a weaver [rolls up the finished web].
He cuts me free from the warp [of the loom];
From day to night You bring me to an end.
AMP.13:
"I lay down until morning.
Like a lion, so He breaks all my bones;
From day until night You bring me to an end.
AMP.14:
"Like a swallow, like a crane, so I chirp;
I coo like a dove.
My eyes look wistfully upward;
O Lord, I am oppressed, take my side and be my security.
AMP.15:
"What shall I say?
For He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done it;
I will wander aimlessly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
AMP.16:
"O Lord, by these things men live,
And in all these is the life of my spirit;
Restore me to health and let me live!
AMP.17:
"Indeed, it was for my own well-being that I had such bitterness;
But You have loved back my life from the pit of nothingness (destruction),
For You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
AMP.18:
"For Sheol cannot praise or thank You,
Death cannot praise You and rejoice in You;
Those who go down to the pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
AMP.19:
"It is the living who give praise and thanks to You, as I do today;
A father tells his sons about Your faithfulness.
AMP.20:
"The LORD is ready to save me;
Therefore we will play my songs on stringed instruments
All the days of our lives at the house of the LORD."
AMP.21: Now Isaiah had said, "Have them take a cake of figs and rub it [as an ointment] on the inflamed spot, that he may recover."
AMP.22: Hezekiah also had said, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"

CSB17.2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
CSB17.3: He said, “Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before you faithfully and wholeheartedly, <sup>ⓚ</sup> and have done what pleases you.” <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
CSB17.4: Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
CSB17.5: “Go and tell Hezekiah, ‘This is what the LORD God of your ancestor David says: I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I am going to add fifteen years to your life. <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.6: And I will rescue you and this city from the grasp of the king of Assyria; I will defend this city. <sup>ⓝ</sup>

CSB17.8: I am going to make the sun’s shadow that goes down on the stairway of Ahaz go back by ten steps.’” <sup>ⓑ</sup> So the sun’s shadow <sup>[6]</sup> went back the ten steps it had descended.

WEB.1: In those days was Hezekiah sick and near death. Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Set your house in order, for you will die, and not live.’”
WEB.2: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to Yahweh,
WEB.3: and said, “Remember now, Yahweh, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” Hezekiah wept bitterly.
WEB.4: Then Yahweh’s word came to Isaiah, saying,
WEB.5: “Go, and tell Hezekiah, ‘Yahweh says, the God of David your father, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
WEB.6: I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
WEB.7: This shall be the sign to you from Yahweh, that Yahweh will do this thing that he has spoken.
WEB.8: Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz with the sun, to return backward ten steps. So the sun returned ten steps on the sundial on which it had gone down.”’”
WEB.9: The writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he had been sick, and had recovered of his sickness.
WEB.10: I said, “In the middle of my life I go into the gates of Sheol.  I am deprived of the residue of my years.”
WEB.11: I said, “I won’t see Yah, Yah in the land of the living. I will see man no more with the inhabitants of the world.
WEB.12: My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up, like a weaver, my life. He will cut me off from the loom. From day even to night you will make an end of me.
WEB.13: I waited patiently until morning. He breaks all my bones like a lion. From day even to night you will make an end of me.
WEB.14: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security.”
WEB.15: What will I say? He has both spoken to me, and himself has done it. I will walk carefully all my years because of the anguish of my soul.
WEB.16: Lord, men live by these things; and my spirit finds life in all of them: you restore me, and cause me to live.
WEB.17: Behold, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.
WEB.18: For Sheol  can’t praise you. Death can’t celebrate you. Those who go down into the pit can’t hope for your truth.
WEB.19: The living, the living, he shall praise you, as I do today. The father shall make known your truth to the children.
WEB.20: Yahweh will save me. Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our life in Yahweh’s house.

NLT.1: About that time Hezekiah became deathly ill, and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz went to visit him. He gave the king this message: “This is what the LORD says: ‘Set your affairs in order, for you are going to die. You will not recover from this illness.’”
NLT.2: When Hezekiah heard this, he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
NLT.3: “Remember, O LORD, how I have always been faithful to you and have served you single-mindedly, always doing what pleases you.” Then he broke down and wept bitterly.
NLT.4: Then this message came to Isaiah from the LORD:
NLT.5: “Go back to Hezekiah and tell him, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I will add fifteen years to your life,
NLT.6: and I will rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria. Yes, I will defend this city.
NLT.7: “‘And this is the sign from the LORD to prove that he will do as he promised:
NLT.8: I will cause the sun’s shadow to move ten steps backward on the sundial of Ahaz!’” So the shadow on the sundial moved backward ten steps.
NLT.9: When King Hezekiah was well again, he wrote this poem:
NLT.10:
I said, “In the prime of my life,
must I now enter the place of the dead?
Am I to be robbed of the rest of my years?”
NLT.11:
I said, “Never again will I see the LORD GOD
while still in the land of the living.
Never again will I see my friends
or be with those who live in this world.
NLT.12:
My life has been blown away
like a shepherd’s tent in a storm.
It has been cut short,
as when a weaver cuts cloth from a loom.
Suddenly, my life was over.
NLT.13:
I waited patiently all night,
but I was torn apart as though by lions.
Suddenly, my life was over.
NLT.14:
Delirious, I chattered like a swallow or a crane,
and then I moaned like a mourning dove.
My eyes grew tired of looking to heaven for help.
I am in trouble, Lord. Help me!”
NLT.15:
But what could I say?
For he himself sent this sickness.
Now I will walk humbly throughout my years
because of this anguish I have felt.
NLT.16:
Lord, your discipline is good,
for it leads to life and health.
You restore my health
and allow me to live!
NLT.17:
Yes, this anguish was good for me,
for you have rescued me from death
and forgiven all my sins.
NLT.18:
For the dead cannot praise you;
they cannot raise their voices in praise.
Those who go down to the grave
can no longer hope in your faithfulness.
NLT.19:
Only the living can praise you as I do today.
Each generation tells of your faithfulness to the next.
NLT.20:
Think of it — the LORD is ready to heal me!
I will sing his praises with instruments
every day of my life
in the Temple of the LORD.
NLT.21: Isaiah had said to Hezekiah’s servants, “Make an ointment from figs and spread it over the boil, and Hezekiah will recover.”
NLT.22: And Hezekiah had asked, “What sign will prove that I will go to the Temple of the LORD?”

MSG.1: At that time, Hezekiah got sick. He was about to die. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz visited him and said, "God says, 'Prepare your affairs and your family. This is it: You're going to die. You're not going to get well.' "
MSG.2: Hezekiah turned away from Isaiah and, facing the wall, prayed to God:
MSG.3: "God, please, I beg you: Remember how I've lived my life. I've lived faithfully in your presence, lived out of a heart that was totally yours. You've seen how I've lived, the good that I have done." And Hezekiah wept as he prayed—painful tears.
MSG.5: "Go and speak with Hezekiah. Give him this Message from me, God, the God of your ancestor David: 'I've heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Here's what I'll do: I'll add fifteen years to your life.

MSG.7: " 'And this is your confirming sign, confirming that I, God, will do exactly what I have promised.

In the very prime of life
I have to leave.

is spent in death's waiting room.

No more glimpses of God
in the land of the living,

no more rubbing shoulders with friends.
MSG.12:
This body I inhabit is taken down
and packed away like a camper's tent.
Like a weaver, I've rolled up the carpet of my life
as God cuts me free of the loom
And at day's end sweeps up the scraps and pieces.
MSG.13:
I cry for help until morning.
Like a lion, God pummels and pounds me,
relentlessly finishing me off.
MSG.14:
I squawk like a doomed hen,
moan like a dove.
My eyes ache from looking up for help:
"Master, I'm in trouble! Get me out of this!"
MSG.15:

MSG.16:

MSG.17:

NET.1: In those days Hezekiah was stricken with a terminal illness. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz visited him and told him, “This is what the LORD says, ‘Give instructions to your household, for you are about to die; you will not get well.’”
NET.2: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD,
NET.3: “Please, LORD. Remember how I have served you faithfully and with wholehearted devotion, and how I have carried out your will.” Then Hezekiah wept bitterly.
NET.5: “Go and tell Hezekiah: ‘This is what the LORD God of your ancestor David says: “I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Look, I will add fifteen years to your life,
NET.6: and rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria. I will shield this city.”’”
NET.21: Isaiah ordered, “Let them take a fig cake and apply it to the ulcerated sore and he will get well.”
NET.22: Hezekiah said, “What is the confirming sign that I will go up to the LORD’s temple?” Isaiah replied, “This is your sign from the LORD confirming that the LORD will do what he has said: Look, I will make the shadow go back ten steps on the stairs of Ahaz.” And then the shadow went back ten steps. Hezekiah’s Song of Thanks This is the prayer of King Hezekiah of Judah when he was sick and then recovered from his illness: “I thought, ‘In the middle of my life I must walk through the gates of Sheol, I am deprived of the rest of my years.’ “I thought, ‘I will no longer see the LORD in the land of the living, I will no longer look on humankind with the inhabitants of the world. My dwelling place is removed and taken away from me like a shepherd’s tent. I rolled up my life like a weaver rolls cloth; from the loom he cuts me off. You turn day into night and end my life. I cry out until morning; like a lion he shatters all my bones; you turn day into night and end my life. Like a swallow or a thrush I chirp, I coo like a dove; my eyes grow tired from looking up to the sky. O sovereign master, I am oppressed; help me! What can I say? He has decreed and acted. I will walk slowly all my years because I am overcome with grief. O sovereign master, your decrees can give men life; may years of life be restored to me. Restore my health and preserve my life.’ “Look, the grief I experienced was for my benefit. You delivered me from the pit of oblivion. For you removed all my sins from your sight. Indeed Sheol does not give you thanks; death does not praise you. Those who descend into the pit do not anticipate your faithfulness. The living person, the living person, he gives you thanks, as I do today. A father tells his sons about your faithfulness. The LORD is about to deliver me, and we will celebrate with music for the rest of our lives in the LORD’s temple.”
